title: Global operations strategies
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers the gains a global business gets from global sourcing, economies of scale, learning from other markets and research and development, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Global operations strategies
card: buying materials, parts or services from the cheapest or best suppliers anywhere in the world, not just nearby.
selling to many countries means producing in larger volumes. This can lower the average cost of each unit.
operating in several countries exposes a business to new ideas, customer tastes and ways of working. It can bring these back to its other operations.
a global business can spread the cost of R&D over its sales in many countries. This makes new products and processes easier to pay for.
draft.remember: A global business can source widely, produce at scale, learn from other markets and spread R&D costs.

a.q: A Sydney furniture maker buys timber from the cheapest suppliers in several countries. Which global gain is this?
a.why: Buying inputs from suppliers anywhere in the world is global sourcing. It is not economies of scale, which is about lower unit costs from producing more.
a.clue: Think about where the inputs come from.

b.q: Kora Foods sells in 12 countries. It makes one product for all of them in a single large factory, so each unit costs less to make. Which gain is this?
b.why: Producing one product in larger volumes lowers the average cost of each unit, which is economies of scale. It is not global sourcing, because the case is about how much is made, not where inputs are bought.
b.clue: Focus on the cost of each unit as output grows.
